newsitem.title: UK: Licht ups 96/97 E.European sugar output estimate.
newsitem.headline: Licht ups 96/97 E.European sugar output estimate.

text.p: German statistician F.O. Licht on Wednesday raised its estimate for east European sugar production by 501,000 tonnes to 9.28 million tonnes in raw value terms for 1996/97, mainly due to a bumper crop in Poland.

"In East Europe, though the forecast total of 9.3 million tonnes is still about 400,000 tonnes below the revised figure for last year, it is likely to be about half a million tonnes more than was originally expected," Licht said.
In its second estimate of European 1996/97 beet sugar production, Licht pegged Polish output at 2.39 million tonnes compared with 1.72 million in 1995/96.
The expected improvement in the Polish crop implied a sugar surplus of around 640,000 tonnes but not all of this might be available for export, Licht said.
"Whether all of this would become available for export is doubtful as subsidised export quotas have been set at 133,000 tonnes, raw value in 1996 and 128,000 tonnes in 1997," it said.
In Ukraine, the region's largest producer, sugar output was expected to reach 2.93 million tonnes, below the official estimate of more than 3.0 million.

"Though recent weather conditions have favoured the crop we think this is too high and are currently estimating 2.93 million tonnes, raw value, Licht said. Ukraine produced 3.79 million tonnes in 1995/96.

Russian sugar production was estimated at 1.80 million tonnes after a previous 2.24 million. With consumption forecast at more than 5.0 million tonnes, this pointed to an import requirement of more than 3.0 million, Licht said.

"A large proportion of this will be forthcoming from the Ukraine, though to protect the Russian domestic industry an import quota of 1.5 million tonnes of white sugar has been set with a limit of 1.15 million tonnes from the Ukraine."

Licht cited Russian sources saying Cuban imports would amount to more than one million tonnes of cane raws. Brazilian, Indian and Thai sugar were all in plentiful supply, it said, noting significant surpluses in some east European nations.
